$comment: The CLI's help, one source for `pxsig help <command>`, `pxsig <command> --help` and the MCP's pxsig_help. test/help.test.mjs keeps it in step with the code, docs/cli.md and the dashboard's Help page. `readBy: engine` marks a flag the Rust binary reads, not the npm CLI.

flags.name: project
flags.meaning: The project. Optional inside a project's folder, or when the workspace has one project.

flags.name: all
flags.meaning: Read commands (status, list, stale, a11y, history, doctor): every project in the workspace. `check --all` keeps its own meaning: every entry.

flags.name: workspace
flags.meaning: The workspace, for this command and everything it starts.

flags.name: json
flags.meaning: The command's data as one JSON document on stdout; logs go to stderr.

flags.name: plain
flags.meaning: Markdown output: tables, no colour, no redraws. Written for logs and agents.

flags.name: markdown
flags.meaning: Same as --plain.

flags.name: pretty
flags.meaning: Terminal output: colour, aligned tables, links, a spinner.

flags.name: help
flags.meaning: With a command: that command's page. Alone: the command list.

flags.name: version
flags.meaning: The versions of this CLI, the engine it would run and the UI contract, then exit (`pxsig version` is the same). With --json, as data.

flags.name: storybook-url
flags.meaning: Config flag: Storybook's URL for this run.

flags.name: storybook-static
flags.meaning: Config flag: a Storybook build to serve when nothing answers at the URL.

flags.name: storybook-config
flags.meaning: Config flag: Storybook's config folder.

flags.name: grid
flags.meaning: Config flag: the signature grid, cells per side.

flags.name: min-cell-px
flags.meaning: Config flag: the adaptive grid's smallest cell.

flags.name: settle-ms
flags.meaning: Config flag: the minimum wait after fonts load.

flags.name: browser
flags.meaning: Config flag: render with this Playwright browser server instead of launching a browser here, usually the container's from `pxsig browser start`.

status.summary: Overview: counts per state, accessibility totals, the most-changed components, the server, staleness. The default command.

flags.meaning: Warn mode for this run, for the named gates (comma-separated; all without a value): a failure in them is reported and exits advisoryExit. A person at a terminal only (exit 3 otherwise); a team sets warn in pxsig.config.json (enforcement).

flags.name: enforce
flags.meaning: Enforce the named gates (all without a value) whatever the config says. Anyone may raise a gate; PXSIG_ENFORCEMENT=enforce does the same.

exits.0: No stale verdicts, or warn mode: the stale gate is on warn (advisoryExit, default 0)

check.summary: Re-render and re-check entries: some through the running server, or the full check. Never writes baselines unless --update is given by a person.
usage: pxsig check --full [--suite name] [--since <ref> | --changed a,b] [--modes a,b] [--only id,id] [--concurrency 8] [--retries 2] [--no-a11y] [--link-base <url>] [--out <name>] [--no-server] [--strict-env] [--sarif file] [--warn[=gates]] [--enforce[=gates]] [--update [--kind word] [--reason text]]

flags.name: changed
flags.meaning: The entries these comma-separated files affect.

flags.name: since
flags.meaning: The entries the changes since <ref> affect (committed, staged, unstaged and untracked).

flags.name: all
flags.meaning: Every entry.

flags.name: full
flags.meaning: The full check: render every selected entry, write check.json, summary.md and junit.xml. `--update`, `--suite` and `--modes` take this path too.

flags.name: suite
flags.meaning: Check manifest.<suite>.json.

flags.name: modes
flags.meaning: Only these modes.

flags.name: only
flags.meaning: Only these entry or story ids. A story not in the manifest yet is registered first.

flags.name: concurrency
flags.meaning: Browser pages rendering in parallel.

flags.name: retries
flags.meaning: Re-render failures up to n times; a pass on retry is flaky.

flags.name: no-a11y
flags.meaning: Skip axe.

flags.name: link-base
flags.meaning: Dashboard URL; summary.md links each entry to <url>#inspect=<id>.

flags.name: out
flags.meaning: Report file name (<store>/reports/<name>.json).

flags.name: no-server
flags.meaning: Do not hand the check to the server: when the server holds the store, refuse instead of queueing on it.

flags.name: timeout-s
flags.meaning: Seconds to wait for the server's queue to drain when the check was handed to it.

flags.name: strict-env
flags.meaning: Refuse (exit 2, nothing rendered) when a selected baseline was approved in a different render environment. Also config env.strict and PXSIG_STRICT_ENV=1. Without it, a difference is a warning. Not applied to --update.

flags.name: update
flags.meaning: Write baselines from the renders instead of checking. A person at a terminal only, after typing UPDATE <n> BASELINES.

flags.name: kind
flags.meaning: With --update: the kind written on each log line (lower case, up to 16 characters). environment re-takes baselines for a new render environment and leaves the accepted a11y list as it is.

flags.name: reason
flags.meaning: With --update: the reason written on each log line, instead of "pxsig check --update".

flags.name: sarif
flags.meaning: With --full: also write the new axe violations (not on an entry's accepted list) as SARIF 2.1.0, for code-scanning viewers. Changes no exit code.

flags.name: warn
flags.meaning: Warn mode for this run, for the named gates (comma-separated; all without a value): a failure in them is reported and exits advisoryExit. A person at a terminal only (exit 3 otherwise); a team sets warn in pxsig.config.json (enforcement).

flags.name: enforce
flags.meaning: Enforce the named gates (all without a value) whatever the config says. Anyone may raise a gate; PXSIG_ENFORCEMENT=enforce does the same.

exits.0: Every checked entry passed, or warn mode: only gates on warn would have failed (advisoryExit, default 0; the ADVISORY lines say what)
exits.1: At least one entry changed, is new or failed to render
exits.2: Usage or setup error, Storybook unreachable, the store locked, or (--strict-env) baselines from a different render environment
exits.3: --update without a person at a terminal

a11y.summary: axe violations per entry, grouped by rule; with --prune, the accepted rules that no longer fire.

flags.name: component
flags.meaning: Entries whose id contains this text.

flags.meaning: Only violations not in the a11y baseline.

flags.name: limit
flags.meaning: Rows shown.

flags.name: prune
flags.meaning: Accepted rules (a11y.json) that a fresh check shows no longer fire. Each accepted rule is prunable, still-fires, stale or not-covered. Removing them is a person's, at a terminal, after typing PRUNE <n> RULES; each entry's removal is logged in a11y-decisions.ndjson.

flags.name: dry-run
flags.meaning: With --prune: list, write nothing. Anyone may run it, assistants included.

flags.name: mode
flags.meaning: With --prune: entries of this mode only.

flags.name: only
flags.meaning: With --prune: these entries only.

flags.name: reason
flags.meaning: With --prune: why, written on each log line.

flags.name: sarif
flags.meaning: Write the new violations of the last report as SARIF 2.1.0 (with --component: that component's). Changes no exit code.

exits.1: --prune: not confirmed, or a decision was made since the plan: nothing written
exits.3: --prune without a person at a terminal

flags.name: component
flags.meaning: Components whose name contains this text.

flags.name: status
flags.meaning: Only these integrity codes.

flags.name: ci
flags.meaning: Fail only on error-severity codes (same as --fail-on error).

flags.name: fail-on
flags.meaning: The lowest severity that makes the exit 1.

flags.name: offline
flags.meaning: Do not fetch the Storybook index; scan the story files instead.

flags.name: limit
flags.meaning: Components shown.

flags.name: repair
flags.meaning: Plan the safe repairs.

flags.name: only
flags.meaning: Limit the repairs to these actions. log-torn runs only when named.

flags.name: apply
flags.meaning: Run the planned repairs. Takes the store lock.

flags.name: prune
flags.meaning: With --repair --apply: move orphans to <store>/trash/. A person at a terminal, after a typed phrase.

flags.name: stale
flags.meaning: Also re-check stale verdicts (left out by default).

flags.name: warn
flags.meaning: Warn mode for this run, for the named gates (comma-separated; all without a value): a failure in them is reported and exits advisoryExit. A person at a terminal only (exit 3 otherwise); a team sets warn in pxsig.config.json (enforcement).

flags.name: enforce
flags.meaning: Enforce the named gates (all without a value) whatever the config says. Anyone may raise a gate; PXSIG_ENFORCEMENT=enforce does the same.

exits.0: Nothing at or above --fail-on, or warn mode: only the doctor gate on warn would have failed (advisoryExit, default 0)
exits.3: --prune or log-torn without a person at a terminal

approve.summary: The guarded way to accept many changes at once: plan, then a person applies. Every approval is logged.

plan.summary: Classify each selected change as colour or shape, block shape changes and stale verdicts, pin every render's hash, write approval-plan.json. Safe for anyone.

flags.name: component
flags.meaning: The changed entries whose id contains this text.

flags.name: all-changed
flags.meaning: Every changed entry.

flags.name: new
flags.meaning: The NEW entries (no baseline yet, with a latest render).

flags.name: reason
flags.meaning: Why: at least eight characters, logged with every approval.

flags.name: allow-shape
flags.meaning: Shape changes allowed in this plan.

flags.name: first-baselines
flags.meaning: With --new: allow every first baseline at once.

exits.2: Nothing to plan, no --reason, usage or setup error

apply.summary: A person at a terminal applies the plan through the server, after typing APPROVE <n> ENTRIES. Refused when any render changed since planning or an entry is no longer in the manifest.

exits.1: Not confirmed, or only part applied (the undo command is printed)
exits.2: The plan is refused (a render changed, or it is over 24 h old), no server, usage or setup error
exits.3: Not a person at a terminal

verify.summary: Baselines whose bytes differ from their last logged approval, baselines with no log line (strict, the default), approvals a crash interrupted, and with --since a rewritten log.

flags.name: no-strict
flags.meaning: Report baselines with no log line without failing (the default before 0.4.0).

flags.name: since
flags.meaning: Also fail when approvals.ndjson at the merge base with <ref> is not a byte prefix of today's (the log was rewritten), or when there is no merge base.

flags.name: suite
flags.meaning: Verify that suite's manifest instead of the main one.

flags.name: all-suites
flags.meaning: Verify the main manifest and every suite; a suite whose manifest is not in this checkout is listed as not committed.

flags.name: adopt
flags.meaning: Log the current baselines (of the manifests named by --suite / --all-suites, else the main one) as the starting point. A person at a terminal.

flags.name: warn
flags.meaning: Warn mode for this run, for the named gates (comma-separated; all without a value): a failure in them is reported and exits advisoryExit. A person at a terminal only (exit 3 otherwise); a team sets warn in pxsig.config.json (enforcement).

flags.name: enforce
flags.meaning: Enforce the named gates (all without a value) whatever the config says. Anyone may raise a gate; PXSIG_ENFORCEMENT=enforce does the same.

exits.0: Every baseline matches the log; or warn mode: only baselines without a log line, with the verify gate on warn (advisoryExit, default 0). A mismatch or a rewritten log fails in every mode
exits.1: A mismatch, an interrupted approval, a baseline with no log line (unless --no-strict), a rewritten log or no merge base (--since), or --adopt not confirmed
exits.2: Usage or setup error, or --since is not a commit
exits.3: --adopt without a person at a terminal

flags.name: ui
flags.meaning: The adapter, for the components each screen leaves to fallbacks and its contract version (default: the one the build records).

flags.name: build
flags.meaning: The adapter build to check (pxsig dashboard build writes it).

flags.name: out
flags.meaning: Where the gallery (index.html), report.json, summary.md and screenshots go.

flags.name: reference
flags.default: the prebuilt dashboard in the pxsig package
flags.meaning: The dashboard each screen is set beside. Without a built one there (a source checkout, a release dry run), the gallery has no reference column and says why.

flags.name: themes
flags.meaning: The themes to render each screen in.

flags.name: only
flags.meaning: Feature ids (comma-separated, from docs/ui/features.md): check only these.

flags.name: strict
flags.meaning: Any axe violation fails the check (exit 1); without it they are listed and advisory.

exits.0: Every screen rendered with no page error
exits.1: A screen did not render, or (with --strict) an axe violation
